SMTO-SKL-0178 — SMTO isn't sure if the GitHub automation started

GUID: 582f4556-e996-53fe-beae-658a5e5232ed
Slug: github-workflow-dispatch-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO asked GitHub to start an automation (a GitHub Actions workflow), but never got a clear answer back. The automation may already be running, so starting it again could run it twice.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On github.com, open the Actions tab, select this automation, and look for a run on the same branch that started around the time you asked. GitHub may have started the run even though SMTO didn't get the confirmation.
  2. If you see that run, don't start the automation again. Follow that run on GitHub, or ask the Agent to check its status. Starting it again would run the same automation twice, which might deploy or publish twice.
  3. Only if no such run appears after a few minutes, ask the Agent to start the automation once more. A run can take a short while to show up on GitHub after it is requested.

What success looks like

  • Exactly one run for this request appears in the Actions tab and the Agent can report its status.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who maintains this automation. If you see two runs, tell them, and don't cancel either until they decide.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The workflow_dispatch request lost its response, or GitHub's reply lacked a positive integer workflow_run_id, so SMTO cannot tell whether a run was started; the dispatch may have been applied.

What this means

  • Workflow dispatch loses a reliable write result or returns no positive integer workflow_run_id. The write may have applied despite its missing or invalid acknowledgement. Read exact provider state and reconcile it before another mutation; matching text alone does not prove attribution.

Why this can happen

  • Workflow dispatch loses a reliable write result or returns no positive integer workflow_run_id.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact workflow/ref, request time and provider run evidence without claiming attribution from matching text.

How to fix it

  • Do not dispatch again. Inspect workflow runs for the exact workflow and ref around the request time (github.workflow_runs or the Actions tab). A run with matching workflow, branch and timing is likely but not proven to come from this request; only dispatch once more after confirming no such run exists.
  • Do not dispatch again. Inspect workflow runs for the exact workflow/ref and request time; ambiguous or matching text alone cannot prove attribution.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not dispatch again. Inspect workflow runs for the exact workflow/ref and request time; ambiguous or matching text alone cannot prove attribution.

How to verify the fix

  • The original dispatch outcome is reconciled before another dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The write may have applied despite its missing or invalid acknowledgement. Read exact provider state and reconcile it before another mutation; matching text alone does not prove attribution.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
